doc.name: storageprices
doc.instructions: StoragePrices exposes read-only Australian self-storage pricing. Use 'search' + 'fetch' for suburb discovery, or call the typed tools directly. Promotional advertised rates are never ongoing-rate claims: inspect is_promotional, standard_price_monthly_aud, promo_duration, ongoing_price_known, and price_disclosure. Never annualise an intro price unless twelve_month_cost_calculable is true. Every tool reads AVAILABLE units by default — the same set storageprices.au shows a human. Pass available_only=false for latest-known rows including units the source stopped listing. Being listed is not live stock: never claim live availability or guaranteed booking prices. CONTRACT: rate limit 20/minute anonymous, 120/minute with a connect token; batch max 3 calls. Errors: (1) JSON-RPC -32602 with data {field,value,allowed|hint|one_of} — fix that argument, do not retry unchanged; (2) isError result {error_code:'handler_error',message,retryable}; (3) isError result {error_code:'timeout',retryable:true,hint}. Row caps: 25-50 rows per call anonymous; a connect token (/mcp/<token>) lifts every tool to 500 — limit_applied and cap_reason say when you were capped. Prefer booking_handoff_url over url when linking a user to book. observed_at is a scrape time, not live availability. place.match_type and place.ambiguous say how a place name resolved. Pass a fetch document's metadata.typed_tool_args verbatim to the tools in its typed_tool_args_for. Full contract: resource storageprices://contract (also GET /mcp-info).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search StoragePrices for Australian suburbs that have self-storage pricing data. Returns a list of matching suburb documents (id, title, url). Use the returned id with the 'fetch' tool to get a full pricing snapshot. When no published suburb page matches, it falls back to facility suburbs that have current prices and returns those as 'place:<state>:<slug>' ids with result_scope='facilities_only' (e.g. 'place:nsw:bondi-junction') — still fetchable, just without a suburb page behind them. Generic words (storage, prices, cheapest, ...) and state names are stripped first, so 'storage prices sydney' finds the Sydney city scope ('city:nsw:sydney', result_scope='city_scope'); a place with a centre but no data of its own returns its priced neighbours with result_scope='nearby' and distance_km. An empty result always carries `suggestions` (never empty): the nearest published suburbs with distance_km when the query could be placed, else the capital-city scopes and 'index:national' — all fetchable ids; `suggestions_basis` says which. Every hit carries suburb, state and match_type (exact, token = a whole word of a longer name, or prefix), exact first. A name that lives in several states is listed in each, with ambiguous=true and ambiguity_note; a catalogue suburb with no page is result_scope='catalogue_unpublished'. result_scope says what kind of place an id names; the same string is still sent as `coverage` on search hits and fetch documents, deprecated: read result_scope. A place that only contains the query inside a longer word is never a result: it is a suggestion, and other_state_matches names where the exact name exists.

query.description: Suburb name or partial text to search for.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Anonymous callers are capped at 25-50 depending on the tool; a valid API key lifts the ceiling to 500. Values above your ceiling are clamped, not rejected.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch the full self-storage pricing snapshot for a document id returned by 'search' — a published suburb page ('suburb:nsw:chatswood'), a facility suburb ('place:nsw:bondi-junction', answered as a 5 km radius snapshot around the centroid of the facilities recorded there — result_scope='nearby' when those facilities carry no current prices), a capital-city scope ('city:nsw:sydney', answered as the city-radius snapshot plus the city's Storage Box Index figure), or 'index:national' (the national Storage Box Index figure and the city-scope ids). metadata carries suburb, state, the scope's facility_count, unit_count, medians and observed_at, a dated citation_text, and typed_tool_args: pass these verbatim to any tool in metadata.typed_tool_args_for (a suburb or city document lists cheapest_storage / compare_prices / storage_near among others; a locality document lists price_distribution only) to continue on the same place and scope. typed_tool_args is null when the document is not a place. result_scope says what kind of document this is; the same string is still sent as `coverage`, deprecated: read result_scope. A row with no verified link has booking_handoff_url null and booking_handoff_reason: 'no operator URL on file' or 'operator URL host is not on the verified booking allow-list'. Link users with booking_handoff_url (tracked, live booking page); url is the StoragePrices page.

id.description: Document id from a search result.

tools.name: cheapest_storage
tools.description: Cheapest observed advertised monthly self-storage prices for a suburb/state and/or size bracket. Optionally constrain by a max monthly price and/or unit floor area (sqm) — e.g. 'cheapest unit under $300 but more than 3 sqm in Fairfield, NSW'. Returns ranked facilities with prices and source URLs (chart-ready). Separately reports the lowest advertised price now and the lowest known ongoing price; intro rates with undisclosed reversion terms are labelled. Rows below the implausibly-cheap floor are excluded from the rows and the market population. A row is below it when its advertised rate is under $5, or when its ongoing rate (the advertised rate if none is known) is under $7 per square metre of unit area, capped at the per-size floor (locker $20, small $20, medium $30, large $50, extra_large $80, garage_plus $50, vehicle $30). A row with no recorded area is held to the per-size floor. Rows with no recorded size and only a category name (large warehouse, office, other, small warehouse, warehouse) are left out too: their prices are unreliable. Every row carries distance_km from the suburb centre, and the `catchment` object states the scope and the farthest result: the market is the suburb page's catchment, not a fixed radius, so a result can sit well outside the suburb. Reads available units by default — the same set storageprices.au shows a human; pass available_only=false for latest-known rows including units the source has stopped listing. For every unit with a non-null booking_handoff_url, include it as a Markdown link labelled ‘Check availability & book’ and preserve the URL exactly. Render that result's commercial_disclosure immediately beside the action link. Clearly show introductory and ongoing prices. When booking_handoff_url is null, use the provided ‘View facility’ action instead. Requires at least one of: suburb, state, size_bracket. A row with no verified link has booking_handoff_url null and booking_handoff_reason: 'no operator URL on file' or 'operator URL host is not on the verified booking allow-list'. Link users with booking_handoff_url (tracked, live booking page); url is the StoragePrices page.

Capital cities (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Canberra, Hobart, Darwin, Gold Coast) resolve to a city-wide radius scope. On price_distribution, an otherwise-empty exact Australian locality can resolve from the packaged ABS SAL snapshot even when StoragePrices has no prices there. Every answer states how the place resolved in `place`. `place.match_type` says how the name matched (exact, token or prefix, ...); when `place.ambiguous` is true the name also matches the places in `place.other_candidates` — confirm with the user or pass state.

max_area_m2.description: Only include units with at most this floor area in square metres. 0 means no area filter. An area bound excludes units whose area is unknown; filters_applied.dropped_unknown_area counts them.

stay_months.description: Requested stay in whole months (1-36). Used to calculate the rent component only when captured promotion duration and ongoing-price terms make that calculation reliable.

tools.name: operator_benchmark
tools.description: For SELF-STORAGE OPERATORS checking their OWN pricing. Give your advertised monthly rate and a market; returns whether you're below / above / aligned with the local median per unit size, the %-distance, the annualised $ per unit you're leaving on the table (or charging over), and your rank vs nearby competitors. Omit size_bracket to sweep all unit sizes at once. Use for 'am I underpriced / overpriced / leaving money on the table / can I raise my rates'. Advertised public rates only — not occupancy or RevPAM. A market needs 3 competitor facilities and 3 observations; below that the status is insufficient_data. Omit my_monthly_price_aud if the user has not stated a price. Never invent one. Without a price the answer is the market median per unit size with verdict=null and a next_step. Pass provider or facility (the operator's own brand) so their own units are excluded from the competitor set. Rows below the implausibly-cheap floor are excluded from the rows and the market population. A row is below it when its advertised rate is under $5, or when its ongoing rate (the advertised rate if none is known) is under $7 per square metre of unit area, capped at the per-size floor (locker $20, small $20, medium $30, large $50, extra_large $80, garage_plus $50, vehicle $30). A row with no recorded area is held to the per-size floor. Rows with no recorded size and only a category name (large warehouse, office, other, small warehouse, warehouse) are left out too: their prices are unreliable.

my_price_is_promotional.description: True when my_monthly_price_aud is an introductory/promotional rate. When omitted the price is treated as ongoing and the answer says assumed_ongoing=true.

my_ongoing_price_aud.description: Known post-promotion ongoing monthly rate (AUD), if publicly disclosed.

size_bracket.description: Unit size to benchmark. Omit to benchmark all sizes at once.

Promo-inclusive facility points are explicitly labelled. Requires at least one of: suburb, state, size_bracket.

tools.description: Add provider (for example storage_king) for provider history: ongoing and advertised monthly series, typical matched-facility movement and rising/falling counts, with explicit coverage gates. Provider-only queries are allowed and return separate size panels, never an all-size median. Storage King and National reconstruct products from historical booking links; other providers have descriptive history but no supported matched headline. A failed coverage gate returns insufficient_comparable_history, never a fallback price movement. Provider history defaults to monthly full UTC periods; use facility_id for a single facility. Without provider, returns the existing market trend: median advertised monthly price per week or month over a lookback window, plus the promotional share each period. Use for 'are prices going up?', seasonality, and promo cycles. Returns a chart-ready time series. trend_summary.direction follows the like-for-like matched panel (direction_basis) and keeps the raw change as advertised_change_pct. National and state-level series are cached for ten minutes (cached, cache_age_s). A query that overruns its statement timeout returns error_code='timeout' with retryable=true — narrow lookback_days or add state/suburb. Requires at least one of: suburb, state, size_bracket, provider.

provider.description: Provider slug or name, e.g. storage_king / Storage King. Enables provider history.

facility_id.description: Optional exact facility ID, within provider. Requires provider; any geography also intersects this filter.

suburb.description: Australian suburb name, e.g. 'Chatswood'. A trailing state or postcode is peeled ('Sydney 2000'). Capital cities (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Canberra, Hobart, Darwin, Gold Coast) resolve to a city-wide radius scope. On price_distribution, an otherwise-empty exact Australian locality can resolve from the packaged ABS SAL snapshot even when StoragePrices has no prices there. Every answer states how the place resolved in `place`. `place.match_type` says how the name matched (exact, token or prefix, ...); when `place.ambiguous` is true the name also matches the places in `place.other_candidates` — confirm with the user or pass state.

lookback_days.description: How far back to look, in days (default 180, max 1095). Values outside 7–1095 are clamped; lookback_days_requested / _applied echo both.

granularity.description: Time bucket size (default month for provider history, week for market history).

tools.name: inferred_market_rate
tools.description: Inferred market ASKING-rate range ($/m²/yr) for self-storage by size band and location: a plain median of asking $/m²/yr from public advertised standard rates, promo-haircut 0.95 (floor). States radius_facility_count and nearest_priced_facility_km; when fewer than 8 comparable facilities sit inside the radius the headline falls back to the state pool and is flagged (fallback, headline_is_fallback, confidence='insufficient') — not a local rate. A market screen — not achieved rent, occupancy, or valuation.

lat.description: Latitude of the location to query (required). Decimal degrees inside Australia, e.g. -33.796.

lng.description: Longitude of the location to query (required). Decimal degrees inside Australia, e.g. 151.183.

size_bracket.description: Storage unit size bracket (required). One of: locker, small, medium, large, extra_large, garage_plus, vehicle.

radius_km.description: Radius to search for comparable facilities in kilometres (default 5). Must be greater than 0. A value below 1 is clamped to 1 and a value above 50 is clamped to 50, never rejected: radius_applied_km states the radius that ran and radius_note says when it was clamped.

resources.name: storageprices_verdict
resources.title: StoragePrices cheapest-storage verdict card
resources.description: Self-contained HTML card (MCP App) that renders the `verdict` block of a cheapest_storage result: the cheapest advertised rate, where it sits in the local market, and a shortlist. For hosts that render UI resources; it carries no data of its own.

resources.name: storageprices_contract
resources.title: StoragePrices connector contract
resources.description: Machine-readable contract for this connector: rate limits, JSON-RPC batch cap, the error shapes (-32602 data, handler_error, timeout), per-tool row caps and how a connect token lifts them, which link to give a user, the REST-to-MCP row field map, and the payload fields a client branches on (place.match_type, search result_scope, fetch typed_tool_args, index_scope, booking_handoff_reason). Read this before answering questions about limits, errors or integration.
